title: Say It in Order
story: A shop sign has several lines: the shop name, what it sells, and the opening hours. If the lines were jumbled, the sign would still be readable - but the meaning would be off. Programs work the same way: one line at a time, in the order you write them.
why: Before adding numbers and decisions, get comfortable with the simplest idea of all: a program is a list of instructions that the computer follows from top to bottom.
analogy: Instructions are like a recipe: step 1, then step 2, then step 3. Swap the steps and you get a different dish.
expected_output:
My favorite things:
Food: pizza
Game: chess
Color: blue
try_it: Add a fourth line to the program. Then move the second line to the end and run it again - watch the output follow your new order.
tips: The computer runs your instructions in the order you write them.
Text goes inside double quotes `"..."` and every instruction ends with `;`.
common_mistakes: Writing two messages inside one `io.println` separated by commas - use one call per line.
Forgetting the `;` at the end of a line.
Expecting the computer to sort or reorder your lines - it never does.
